description: Graduate Engineering students interested in space, AI/ML, and remote sensing. Looking for participants interested in satellite data, GIS, Python/data analysis, visualization, or web development to join my NASA Space Apps team and work on the Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots challenge. Looking for curious, collaborative people excited to build an innovative solution!
summary: FIREVERSE is a web application that harmonizes NASA FIRMS active-fire detections from MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) into one consistent record, so that each fire is counted once. It links detections of the same fire across sensors by footprint overlap and time, then presents the result as a burning activity calendar, map, 3D globe and historical analysis for any region, with unusual periods compared against a 2003-2025 MODIS baseline. It then goes one step further and asks what the smoke is about to cross: a plume model driven by observed fire power and modelled wind shows which power lines, roads, clinics and schools are downwind. Seven simple role pages (fire brigade, grid operator, road patrol, driver, clinic lead, resident, analyst) turn this into one-screen answers and shareable bulletins in English, Spanish and Portuguese for Paraguay, Bolivia, Argentina and Brazil. Every value is labelled observed, mapped, modelled or scenario, and nothing is invented. This matters because responders need a comparable fire record and a fast, honest answer about who is downwind.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

FIREVERSE has three layers.

1. Harmonization. MODIS and VIIRS detections from NASA FIRMS are normalized to one schema (time, location, fire radiative power, confidence class, footprint). Detections of the same fire are linked across sensors by footprint overlap within a time window, so duplicates are counted once. The Hot Spot Explorer shows the harmonized record as a map, a 3D globe, a burning activity calendar, a historical analysis against a 2003-2025 MODIS baseline, and a data table for any region. A Harmonization Lab shows how records were matched.

2. Smoke. FIRELAB runs a Gaussian plume for any detected fire from its observed fire radiative power and modelled wind, hour by hour. DOWNWIND applies it to every recent fire and lists the power lines, main roads, clinics and schools in the modelled smoke path. It also flags fires that are close but not downwind, which a simple distance ring would get wrong.

3. People. Seven role pages (fire brigade, grid operator, road patrol, driver, clinic or school lead, resident, analyst) give one-screen answers, a three-step shift briefing, and bulletins in full or SMS length that can be copied, read aloud or shared by WhatsApp, in English, Spanish and Portuguese. A smoke-aware route planner compares driving routes by the modelled smoke on each at the time of travel, searches for a detour, gives turn-by-turn directions with smoke warnings, and hands the route to Google Maps or exports GeoJSON for map providers.

VALIDATION AND LIMITS

We replayed a real event: on 8 January 2025 a 500 kV line in Paraguay tripped and the utility attributed it to smoke. Satellites had detected fires nearby before the trip, and the modelled smoke crosses a 500 kV line in two places. The replay cannot show which fire caused the trip and it gave no same-day warning; the page says so. In a full-year test for 2025, a wind-aware rule did not reduce alert days compared with a distance ring; it changes which fires are ranked first. Every value is labelled OBSERVED, MAPPED, MODELLED or SCENARIO. Smoke values are scenarios, not measurements, and no detection does not mean no fire. The bundled data is a snapshot from 6 to 13 November 2026.

IMPACT

A consistent fire record for analysts, and a fast, honest answer for the people downwind. It covers Paraguay, Bolivia, Argentina and Brazil today; another country is one configuration entry.

TOOLS

Python (standard-library web server, pandas, numpy), vanilla JavaScript, Leaflet, Chart.js, no build step. Tests: pytest, Node unit tests and Playwright browser checks in Chrome.

AI DISCLOSURE

Code, documentation and this text were written with AI coding assistance (Claude) and reviewed by the team. In the demo video, the narration voice and the character art are AI-generated and labelled on screen; the app screens are real.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS: MODIS (Terra, Aqua) and VIIRS (S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) active fire detections
NASA FIRMS archive download (MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS 375 m country archives, 2003-2025)
projectRefs: Open-Meteo: modelled wind, boundary-layer height, ERA5 reanalysis and CAMS PM2.5
OpenStreetMap: power lines, roads, clinics, schools and places (via Overpass API)
OSRM: driving routes for the smoke-aware route planner
INPE Programa Queimadas (Brazil): 10-minute GOES-19 fire detections for the fast look
NOAA GOES-16 fire product on AWS Open Data, used in the January 2025 replay
GHSL GHS-POP population grid (European Commission JRC) for exposure estimates
Playwright: browser tests and demo recording
edge-tts: AI-generated narration voice in the demo video
Claude (Anthropic): AI coding and writing assistance
